questions.question: The 15th edition of the India‑Vietnam Defence Policy Dialogue (DPD) was held in which of the following cities in November 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hanoi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **15th edition** of the **India-Vietnam Defence Policy Dialogue (DPD)** was scheduled to be held in **Hanoi**, **Vietnam**, in **November 2025**.
 
• This high-level dialogue serves as a cornerstone for reviewing the progress of **bilateral defence cooperation** between the two nations, which have historically shared strong ties.
 
• The meeting is typically co-chaired by the **Defence Secretary** of **India** and the **Deputy Defence Minister** of **Vietnam**, reflecting the high priority both countries accord to their security partnership.
 
• Key discussions during this **15th edition** focused on deepening collaboration in areas such as **maritime security**, **cyber security**, **military training**, and the **defence industry**.
 
• The dialogue aims to align the strategic interests of both nations in the **Indo-Pacific region**, ensuring a stable and rules-based international order. ***Hence, the correct answer is Hanoi.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Comprehensive Strategic Partnership:**
 
 
• The relationship between **India** and **Vietnam** was upgraded to a **Comprehensive Strategic Partnership** in **September 2016** during the visit of the Indian Prime Minister to **Vietnam**.
 
• This status is **Vietnam's** highest tier of diplomatic partnership, shared with only a few other countries like **Russia**, **China**, and **South Korea**.
 
 
 
• **Joint Vision Statement 2030:**
 
 
• During the **13th DPD** and subsequent high-level visits, both nations signed the **"Joint Vision Statement on India-Vietnam Defence Partnership towards 2030"**.
 
• This document significantly enhances the scope and scale of existing **defence cooperation**, focusing on **mutual logistics support** and **capacity building**.
 
 
 
• **Maritime Security and South China Sea:**
 
 
• **India** and **Vietnam** share common concerns regarding the **freedom of navigation** and overflight in the **South China Sea**.
 
• **India** has consistently supported a peaceful resolution of disputes in the region based on **UNCLOS 1982**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Defence Exercises:** 
 
 
• **VINBAX** is the annual bilateral military exercise between the **Indian Army** and the **Vietnam People’s Army**, which focuses on **UN Peacekeeping Operations** and humanitarian assistance.
 
 
 
• **Line of Credit (LoC):** 
 
 
• **India** extended a **$100 million Defence Line of Credit** to **Vietnam** for the procurement of **12 High-Speed Guard Boats** for the **Vietnam Border Guard**, demonstrating commitment to **Vietnam's** maritime capacity.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:** 
 
 
• Diplomatic relations were established in **1972**, and the two countries celebrated **50 years** of diplomatic ties in **2022**.
 
• Vietnam is a key pillar of **India's Act East Policy** and an essential partner in the **Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative (IPOI)**.

questions.question: What was India’s rank in the 2025 SDG Index released by the UN Sustainable Development Solutions Network?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**99th**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India has achieved the **99th rank** in the **2025 Sustainable Development Report (SDR)**, also known as the **SDG Index**, which evaluates the progress of **167 countries** toward the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**.
 
• The index is released annually by the **UN Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN)**, an organization that has been tracking the performance of **UN member states** since the adoption of the **2030 Agenda** in **2015**.
 
• India’s jump to the **99th position** signifies a notable improvement in its overall score, reflecting advancements in various socio-economic and environmental indicators compared to previous years.
 
• The **2025 report** highlights India's steady progress in areas such as **Goal 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production)** and **Goal 13 (Climate Action)**, although challenges remain in achieving **Goal 2 (Zero Hunger)** and **Goal 5 (Gender Equality)**.
 
• The **Sustainable Development Report** provides a comprehensive data-driven assessment of how close each nation is to achieving the **17 goals** established by the **United Nations General Assembly**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Understanding the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):**
 
 
• The **SDGs** consist of **17 interlinked global goals** designed to be a "blueprint to achieve a better and more sustainable future for all" by the **year 2030**.
 
• These goals were adopted by all **193 UN Member States** in **September 2015** during the **United Nations Sustainable Development Summit**.
 
 
 
• **Global Rankings and Leaders:**
 
 
• In the **2025 Index**, Nordic countries like **Finland**, **Sweden**, and **Denmark** continue to lead the rankings, demonstrating high performance across almost all environmental and social targets.
 
• The report emphasizes that while **developed nations** rank higher, they often generate significant **negative international spillovers** that affect the ability of **developing nations** to reach their goals.
 
 
 
• **India's Internal Monitoring - SDG India Index:**
 
 
• In addition to global rankings, **NITI Aayog** in India publishes the **SDG India Index** to track the performance of **States and Union Territories**.
 
• This domestic index aligns with the **National Indicator Framework (NIF)** and helps foster **competitive federalism** by ranking states like **Kerala**, **Tamil Nadu**, and **Himachal Pradesh** as front-runners in sustainability.
 
 
 
• **The Role of SDSN:**
 
 
• The **UN Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN)** was set up in **2012** under the auspices of the **UN Secretary-General**.
 
• It mobilizes global scientific and technological expertise to promote practical solutions for sustainable development, including the implementation of the **Paris Agreement** on **Climate Change**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Data Facts:** The **SDG Index** uses a scale of **0 to 100**, where **100** represents the optimum score (full goal achievement). India’s progress from being ranked **112th in 2024** (estimated) to **99th in 2025** shows a significant upward trajectory in its **SDG Dashboard**.
 
• **Challenges Identified:** Despite the improved rank, the **2025 report** warns that **global progress** has stalled for the third year in a row due to **geopolitical tensions** and **economic fluctuations** following the **COVID-19 pandemic**.
 
• **Future Targets:** India aims to reach net-zero carbon emissions by **2070**, a commitment made at **COP26**, which remains a critical component of its long-term strategy for **Goal 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy)** and **Goal 13**.

questions.question: In April 2025, at the National Federation Cup Athletics held at Maharaja's College Ground in Ernakulam, which Indian long jumper broke Anju Bobby George's 23-year-old national record with a jump of 6.64 m?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shaili Singh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **April 2025**, the young Indian athlete **Shaili Singh** showcased an exceptional performance at the **National Federation Cup Athletics** championships.
 
• The event was hosted at the **Maharaja's College Ground** in **Ernakulam** (Kochi), **Kerala**, which is a historic venue for track and field events in India.
 
• **Shaili Singh** recorded a massive jump of **6.64 m**, which, according to the competition context, broke a **23-year-old** record previously held by the legendary **Anju Bobby George** at this specific meet. ***Hence, the statement regarding her record-breaking jump is correct.***
 
• She is a protégé of the **Anju Bobby George Foundation** and has been consistently performing at the highest domestic and international levels in the **Long Jump** category.
 
• The **National Federation Cup** serves as a critical selection trial for Indian athletes aiming for international assignments like the **Asian Athletics Championships** and the **World Athletics Championships**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Shaili Singh:**
 
 
• Born on **January 7, 2004**, in **Jhansi**, **Uttar Pradesh**, she is considered one of the brightest prospects in Indian athletics.
 
• She is coached by **Robert Bobby George**, who is the husband and former coach of **Anju Bobby George**.
 
• In **2021**, she won the **Silver Medal** at the **World Athletics U20 Championships** held in **Nairobi**, **Kenya**, with a jump of **6.59 m**.
 
• Her personal best of **6.76 m** (achieved in **2023**) is the **second-longest** jump by an Indian woman, trailing only behind her mentor's national record.
 
 
 
• **Anju Bobby George:**
 
 
• She is the first Indian athlete to win a medal at the **World Championships in Athletics**, securing a **Bronze** in **Paris** in **2003**.
 
• Her national record of **6.83 m** was set at the **2004 Athens Olympics**, where she finished **fifth** (later upgraded to fourth).
 
• She was awarded the **Padma Shri** in **2004** and the **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna** in **2003** for her contributions to sports.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Options Analysis:**
 
 
• **Ancy Sojan:** A talented long jumper from **Kerala** who has been a close competitor to Shaili Singh, frequently crossing the **6.50 m** mark in domestic circuits.
 
• **Priyanka Goswami:** An Indian athlete who specializes in the **20 km Race Walk**. She represented India at the **Tokyo 2020 Olympics** and won a **Silver Medal** at the **2022 Commonwealth Games**.
 
• **D Sudha Singh:** An Indian Olympic athlete who competes in the **3000 m Steeplechase** event. She is an **Asian Games Gold medalist** (**2010 Guangzhou**) and a **two-time Olympian**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the venue:** The **Maharaja's College Ground** in **Ernakulam** is renowned for its synthetic track and has been a breeding ground for several international athletes from **Kerala**.

questions.question: As of August 2025, who among the following was the Governor of the Reserve Bank of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shri Sanjay Malhotra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Shri Sanjay Malhotra** assumed the role of the **Governor** of the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** following the conclusion of the tenure of his predecessor. As of **August 2025**, he continues to lead India's central banking institution.
 
• He is a distinguished **1990-batch Indian Administrative Service (IAS)** officer of the **Rajasthan cadre**. His appointment was cleared by the **Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC)** for a standard tenure of **three years**.
 
• Prior to his elevation as the RBI Governor, he served as the **Secretary** in the **Department of Revenue** under the **Ministry of Finance**, where he played a pivotal role in tax policy and administration.
 
• He took over the reins from **Shaktikanta Das**, who served a significant term including an extension. Shri Malhotra is the **26th Governor** of the **Reserve Bank of India**.
 
• As the Governor, he acts as the **Chief Executive Officer** of the bank and the **ex-officio Chairperson** of the **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)**, which is tasked with maintaining **price stability** and controlling **inflation**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Reserve Bank of India (RBI):** 
 
 
• Established on **April 1, 1935**, under the **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934**, based on the recommendations of the **Hilton Young Commission**.
 
• The **Central Office** was initially in **Kolkata** but was permanently moved to **Mumbai** in **1937**.
 
• The bank was **nationalized** in **1949**, making it fully owned by the **Government of India**.
 
 
 
• **Structure of RBI Governance:**
 
 
• The bank's affairs are governed by a **Central Board of Directors**. This board is appointed by the **Government of India** in keeping with the **Reserve Bank of India Act**.
 
• The board consists of the **Governor** and not more than **four Deputy Governors**, along with non-official directors nominated by the government.
 
 
 
• **Functions of the Governor:**
 
 
• The Governor is responsible for the overall direction and **management** of the bank. He signs the **currency notes** (except the one-rupee note, which is signed by the **Finance Secretary**).
 
• The Governor represents India at various **international forums** such as the **International Monetary Fund (IMF)** and the **Bank for International Settlements (BIS)**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• The first Governor of the RBI was **Sir Osborne Smith** (**1935–1937**).
 
• The first Indian to serve as the Governor was **C.D. Deshmukh** (**1943–1949**).
 
• **Manmohan Singh** is the only **Prime Minister of India** who also served as the **Governor of the RBI** (**1982–1985**).
 
 
 
• **Other Noted Personalities (Options):**
 
 
• **Dr. Poonam Gupta:** She is the **Director General** of the **National Council of Applied Economic Research (NCAER)** and was the first woman to hold this prestigious position.
 
• **Shri Saugata Bhattacharya:** A prominent **economist** who has held senior positions at **Axis Bank** and has been a member of the **PM’s Economic Advisory Council**.
 
• **Dr. Nagesh Kumar:** A renowned economist serving as the **Director** of the **Institute for Studies in Industrial Development (ISID)** and a former Director at **UN-ESCAP**.
 
 
 
• **Key Responsibilities:** The Governor manages **foreign exchange reserves**, acts as a **banker to the government**, and regulates the **banking system** under the **Banking Regulation Act, 1949**.

questions.question: Which significant new financial institution was launched in June 2025 to support India’s maritime economy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sagarmala Finance Corporation Ltd.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **Sagarmala Finance Corporation Ltd.** (**SFCL**) was officially launched in **June 2025** as a dedicated financial institution to provide long-term and low-cost credit to India's **maritime** and **blue economy** sectors.
 
• It functions under the administrative control of the **Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways**, aiming to bridge the massive funding gap in **port-led development** projects.

questions.question: Which tribal poet from Jharkhand received the Sahitya Akademi Yuva Puraskar in June 2025 for ‘Phir Ugna’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Parvati Tirkey**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Parvati Tirkey**, a distinguished tribal poet from **Jharkhand**, was selected for the prestigious **Sahitya Akademi Yuva Puraskar** in **June 2025**.
 
• She received this recognition for her debut collection of poems titled **‘Phir Ugna’**, which is written in **Hindi**.
 
• The collection **‘Phir Ugna’** is noted for its deep exploration of **tribal identity**, the pain of **displacement**, and the symbiotic relationship between **nature and indigenous communities**.
 
• Originally hailing from the **Gumla** district of **Jharkhand**, **Parvati Tirkey** belongs to the **Oraon (Kurukh)** tribe, and her work brings the lived experiences of her community to the forefront of mainstream Indian literature.
 
• The **Sahitya Akademi Yuva Puraskar** is a literary honor in India which the **Sahitya Akademi** annually confers on young writers of outstanding merit in any of the **24 major Indian languages**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sahitya Akademi Yuva Puraskar:**
 
 
• This award was established in **2011** to recognize and promote young authors under the **age of 35**.
 
• The award consists of a **casket** containing an engraved copper plaque and a **purse of Rs. 50,000**.
 
• The selection is made by a **three-member jury** in each language, following a rigorous process of nomination and evaluation.
 
 
 
• **Other Notable Winners Mentioned:**
 
 
• **Akhil P Dharmajan**: A popular writer from **Kerala** who was recognized for his **Malayalam** novel **'Ram C/O Anandhi'**, which gained significant traction on social media.
 
• **Kirtida Brahmbhatt**: An author recognized for her contributions to **Gujarati** literature.
 
• **Mayur Khavdu**: Another recipient honored for his literary work in the **Gujarati** language.
 
 
 
• **Literary Context of Jharkhand:**
 
 
• **Jharkhand** has a rich tradition of **tribal literature** that focuses on **"Jal, Jangal, Jameen"** (Water, Forest, Land).
 
• Poets like **Parvati Tirkey** follow the legacy of other Sahitya Akademi winners from the state, contributing to the **Hindi** and **regional language** literary canons.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Selection Criteria:** To be eligible for the **Yuva Puraskar**, the author must be an **Indian national** and must not have exceeded **35 years of age** as of **January 1st** of the year of the award.
 
• **The Sahitya Akademi:** It was founded on **March 12, 1954**, and is an autonomous organization under the **Ministry of Culture**, Government of India. It is headquartered at **Rabindra Bhavan** in **New Delhi**.
 
• **Scope of Languages:** The Akademi recognizes works in **24 languages**, which include the **22 languages** listed in the **Eighth Schedule** of the **Indian Constitution**, plus **English** and **Rajasthani**.

questions.question: What is the name of India's first humanoid robot developed for space missions, announced in 2023?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Vyommitra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vyommitra** is India's first **humanoid robot** designed specifically for space missions.
 
• It was developed by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)**, showcasing advancements in space technology.
 
• **Vyommitra** is a female humanoid robot that can mimic human actions and perform specific tasks in space environments.
 
• The name **"Vyommitra"** is derived from Sanskrit, where "Vyom" means **space** and "Mitra" means **friend**, symbolizing a "friend in space."
 
• It is intended to be deployed in **unmanned space missions**, including the **Gaganyaan mission**, serving as a precursor to human spaceflight.
 
• The humanoid can perform **crew functions**, like operating control panels, environmental monitoring, and providing feedback to mission controllers.
 
• Vyommitra is equipped with advanced **artificial intelligence** and sensors to interact with astronauts and provide assistance during space missions.
 
• It is designed to handle **microgravity conditions**, making it suitable for tasks in the challenging environment of outer space.
 
• This innovation marks India’s stride in advancing **robotics** and **human-robot interaction** for space exploration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Vikram**__

 __
 
• **Vikram** is the name of the lander used in **Chandrayaan-2**, India’s lunar exploration mission.
 
• It is named after **Dr. Vikram Sarabhai**, the father of the Indian space program.
 
• Vikram was designed to land on the lunar surface and conduct scientific experiments, but it is not a humanoid robot.
 
 
 
• **Suryamitra**__
 __
 
• **Suryamitra** is an initiative by India to train **solar technicians** under the **National Institute of Solar Energy (NISE).**
 
• The program aims to create skilled manpower for the **solar energy sector** in India.
 
• It is not related to space missions or humanoid robotics.
 
 
 
• **Aditya**__
 
 
• **Aditya** is the name of India’s first **solar mission**, also known as **Aditya-L1**.
 
• The mission aims to study the **solar corona**, solar emissions, and other solar phenomena.
 
• It is not a humanoid robot but a spacecraft designed for scientific research on the Sun.

questions.question: Who set a new world indoor 5000 m race walk record at the Italian Indoor Championships in Ancona (Feb 2025)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Francesco Fortunato**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Italian race walker Francesco Fortunato** made history at the **Italian Indoor Championships** held in **Ancona** in **February 2025** by setting a new **World Indoor Record** in the **5000 m race walk**.
 
• He clocked a remarkable time of **18:03.01**, shattering the previous world indoor mark that had stood for three decades.
 
• The previous record of **18:07.08** was held by the **Russian** athlete **Mikhail Shchennikov**, which was set in **1995**.
 
• This performance took place at the **Pala Indoor** stadium in **Ancona**, which is the traditional home for the **Italian Athletics Indoor Championships**.
 
• **Francesco Fortunato** represents the **Fiamme Gialle** (the sports section of the Italian Finance Guard) and has been a consistent performer for **Italy** in international athletics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Profile of Francesco Fortunato:**
 
 
• He was born on **December 13, 1994**, in **Andria, Italy**.
 
• He is a specialist in the **20 km race walk** and has represented **Italy** at the **Tokyo 2020 Olympics** and the **Paris 2024 Olympics**.
 
• His record-breaking feat in **2025** cements his position as one of the fastest walkers in the history of the sport, particularly in the shorter **indoor** formats.
 
 
 
• **Race Walking Mechanics:**
 
 
• Race walking is a long-distance foot race where athletes must always have **one foot in contact with the ground**.
 
• The **advancing leg** must be **straightened** (i.e., not bent at the knee) from the moment of first contact with the ground until the vertical upright position.
 
• Judges monitor these two rules strictly, and **three red cards** lead to disqualification.
 
 
 
• **Other Athletes in the Options:**
 
 
• **Evan Dunfee**: A highly decorated **Canadian** race walker who won the **bronze medal** in the **50 km race walk** at the **Tokyo 2020 Olympics**.
 
• **Toshikazu Yamanishi**: A **Japanese** athlete who is a **two-time World Champion** (**2019 and 2022**) in the **20 km race walk**.
 
• **Matteo Giupponi**: Another prominent **Italian** race walker who won the **bronze medal** at the **2022 European Athletics Championships**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of the Record:** The **5000 m indoor** event is a test of extreme speed and technical precision, often used by outdoor specialists to build **anaerobic capacity** during the **winter season**.
 
• **Venue Facts:** The city of **Ancona**, located in the **Marche region** of **Italy**, hosts the **National Indoor Championships** almost every year due to its state-of-the-art **200-meter banked track** facilities.
 
• **Governing Bodies:** Records in this discipline are ratified by **World Athletics** (formerly **IAAF**) and the **FIDAL** (Federazione Italiana di Atletica Leggera) at the national level.
 
• **Historical Context:** Before **Fortunato's** achievement, the **18-minute barrier** was considered nearly impossible for the **5000 m indoor walk**; his time of **18:03.01** has brought the world closer to that historic milestone.

questions.question: Which data collection method contributed to the accurate poverty estimates in India, as per the SBI report in June 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Modified Mixed Recall Period**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **State Bank of India (SBI)** Research report, released in **June 2025**, highlighted that poverty in India has declined significantly, largely attributed to the updated methodology used in the **Household Consumption Expenditure Survey (HCES) 2022-23**.
 
• The report emphasizes that the shift to the **Modified Mixed Recall Period (MMRP)** has provided a more accurate and realistic estimation of household consumption patterns compared to older methods.
 
• Under the **MMRP**, the **National Sample Survey Office (NSSO)** collects data using three different time frames: a **7-day recall period** for high-frequency items (like edible oil, eggs, fish, fruits, vegetables, and tobacco), a **30-day recall period** for mid-frequency items (fuel, rent, and non-durable goods), and a **365-day recall period** for durable goods (clothing, footwear, and education).
 
• The **SBI report** notes that the **Gini Coefficient**, which measures inequality, has also seen a decline, indicating that economic growth is becoming more inclusive across both **rural** and **urban** sectors.
 
• Based on the **MMRP** data, the report estimates that rural poverty has dropped to around **7.2%** and urban poverty to **4.6%**, bringing the national average to approximately **5%** or lower.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Uniform Recall Period (URP):**
 
 
• In this method, the consumption data for all items is collected for a uniform **30-day recall period**.
 
• This was the primary method used by the **NSSO** until the late **1990s** but was criticized for underestimating the consumption of durable goods and overestimating the consumption of perishables due to recall bias.
 
 
 
• **Mixed Recall Period (MRP):**
 
 
• The **MRP** uses a **365-day recall period** for five low-frequency categories (clothing, footwear, durable goods, education, and institutional medical expenses) and a **30-day recall period** for all other items.
 
• This was the standard used in the **2011-12** poverty estimations but has been superseded by the more granular **MMRP**.
 
 
 
• **Household Consumption Expenditure Survey (HCES):**
 
 
• The **HCES** is conducted by the **National Sample Survey Office (NSSO)** under the **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)**.
 
• The **2022-23 survey** was particularly significant as it was conducted after a gap of **11 years**, following the junking of the **2017-18** survey data.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Recall Periods:**
 
 
• Shorter recall periods (like **7 days**) for food items reduce **memory lapse** and provide more accurate data on nutritional intake.
 
• Longer recall periods for durables prevent "bulky" one-time expenditures from skewing the monthly average consumption.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Economic Impact:** The transition to **MMRP** allows the **Government of India** to recalibrate the **Consumer Price Index (CPI)** basket, as it reflects current consumption habits where the share of **food** in the total budget has declined.
 
• **World Bank Context:** Many international organizations, including the **World Bank** and **International Monetary Fund (IMF)**, monitor these methodological shifts to update **Global Poverty** counts and the **$2.15-a-day** (2017 PPP) poverty line.
 
• **Data Fact:** The **SBI Ecowrap** report specifically mentions that the decline in poverty is a result of **government-led interventions** such as the **PM-GKAY (Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana)**, which provides free food grains to over **80 crore** people.
</ul

questions.question: What approximate percentage of the Union Budget 2025-26 was allocated to gender-specific schemes to address women’s empowerment?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**8.86%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the **Union Budget 2025-26**, presented by Union Finance Minister **Nirmala Sitharaman** on **February 1, 2025**, the allocation for gender-specific schemes reached a historic high of approximately **8.86%** of the total expenditure.
 
• The total outlay for the **Gender Budget Statement (GBS)** for the fiscal year **2025-26** is estimated at **₹4.43 lakh crore**, out of a total projected budget expenditure of **₹50.01 lakh crore**.
 
• This allocation signifies a substantial increase from the previous fiscal year (2024-25), where the gender budget stood at approximately **₹3.10 lakh crore** (around 6.5% of the total budget), reflecting the government's shift toward **women-led development**.
 
• The **Gender Budget** is categorized into two main parts: **Part A**, which includes schemes with 100% allocation for women, and **Part B**, which includes schemes where at least 30% of the allocation is dedicated to women.
 
• The primary objective of this increased funding is to enhance **economic participation**, ensure **safety and security**, and improve the **socio-economic status** of women across both rural and urban sectors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Gender Budgeting in India**: 
 
 
• India formally adopted **Gender Budgeting** in the year **2005-06** to ensure that the benefits of development reach women as much as men.
 
• It is not a separate budget for women but a tool to analyze the **budgetary process** through a gender lens to address disparities.
 
 
 
• **Mission Shakti**: 
 
 
• This is an integrated women empowerment programme launched by the **Ministry of Women and Child Development**.
 
• It consists of two sub-schemes: **'Sambal'** (for safety and security, including One Stop Centres and Beti Bachao Beti Padhao) and **'Samarthya'** (for empowerment, including Ujjwala and Swadhar Greh).
 
 
 
• **Lakhpati Didi Scheme**: 
 
 
• The **Union Budget 2025-26** continued its focus on the **Lakhpati Didi** initiative, aiming to empower **3 crore women** in **Self-Help Groups (SHGs)** to earn an annual income of at least **₹1 lakh**.
 
• As of **2025**, nearly 1 crore women have already achieved this status through various skill development and micro-credit interventions.
 
 
 
• **PM Awas Yojana (Grameen)**: 
 
 
• Under this scheme, a significant portion of the **Gender Budget** is utilized as the government mandates that houses should be owned solely or jointly by **women**, thereby enhancing their **asset-ownership** and social standing.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Economic Impact**: The **8.86%** allocation is distributed across various ministries, including **Rural Development**, **Education**, and **Health**, to support women's health through schemes like **PM Matru Vandana Yojana**.
 
• **Mudra Yojana**: Under the **PM Mudra Yojana**, more than **70% of loans** have been sanctioned to **women entrepreneurs**, fostering financial independence and entrepreneurship at the grassroots level.
 
• **STEM Education**: The budget highlights an increase in the enrollment of women in **STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics)** courses, which currently stands at **43%** in India, one of the highest in the world.
 
• **Safety Initiatives**: Funds under the **Nirbhaya Fund** and dedicated allocations for **women police volunteers** and **fast-track special courts** are crucial components of the security framework funded by the 2025-26 gender budget.

8f:T26

questions.question: In July 2025, the Union Environment Ministry notified the Environment Protection Rules, 2025, for which sites?
questions.solution:
p>The correct answer is __**Chemically Contaminated Sites**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **July 2025**, the **Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)** officially notified the **Environment Protection Rules, 2025**, specifically targeting the management and remediation of **Chemically Contaminated Sites**.
 
• The primary objective of these rules is to provide a comprehensive legal framework for the **identification, investigation, and decontamination** of areas where **hazardous substances** have accumulated in the soil or groundwater.
 
• These rules are issued under the powers conferred by the **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986**, which allows the Central Government to take measures to protect and improve the quality of the environment.
 
• The notification introduces strict protocols for the **Remediation of Contaminated Sites**, ensuring that toxic hotspots do not pose a continued threat to **public health** or the surrounding **ecosystem**.
 
• A significant feature of these rules is the enforcement of the **"Polluter Pays Principle"**, which mandates that the person or organization responsible for the contamination must bear the **financial liability** for the cleanup process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986:** This **parliamentary act** serves as the umbrella legislation for environmental safety in India. It was enacted in the wake of the **Bhopal Gas Tragedy** and gives the government the authority to regulate all forms of **pollution** and coordinate the activities of various central and state authorities.
 
• **Nature of Contaminated Sites:** These sites usually include **abandoned industrial units**, **hazardous waste dumpsites**, and areas near **chemical factories** where toxic chemicals like **heavy metals, mercury, arsenic, or persistent organic pollutants** have leached into the environment.
 
• **Role of Regulatory Bodies:** The **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)** is tasked with maintaining an updated **National Inventory of Contaminated Sites**. Along with the **State Pollution Control Boards (SPCBs)**, it monitors the progress of remediation and ensures compliance with the **2025 Rules**.
 
• **Technological Solutions:** The rules advocate for modern **remediation technologies** such as **bioremediation** (using microorganisms to degrade pollutants), **phytoremediation** (using plants), and **soil washing** to restore the quality of land and water.
 
• **Significance of the Rules:** Prior to this notification, the management of such sites was often fragmented. The **Environment Protection Rules, 2025**, streamline the process, providing clear **threshold values** for contaminants and a structured **timeframe** for completing remediation activities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Identification Process:** The rules specify that a site is classified as **"contaminated"** if the concentration of hazardous substances exceeds the **Screening Levels** prescribed by the **Ministry**.
 
• **Public Health Impact:** These rules are crucial for preventing long-term health issues such as **cancer, neurological disorders, and birth defects** which are often linked to living near **chemically contaminated areas**.
 
• **Global Alignment:** The notification aligns India’s domestic policies with international standards like the **Stockholm Convention** on Persistent Organic Pollutants and the **Minamata Convention** on Mercury.

questions.question: When did/will the new FASTag annual plan become effective in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**15 August 2025**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Highways Authority of India (NHAI)** and **Indian Highway Management Company Limited (IHMCL)** have slated the new **FASTag annual plan** and updated regulations to become fully effective from **15 August 2025**.
 
• This new framework introduces a mandatory **replacement cycle** for **FASTags** that have been in use for more than **5 years**, ensuring the hardware remains functional and technologically up-to-date.
 
• As per the guidelines, all **FASTag users** must ensure their **Know Your Customer (KYC)** details are updated and verified before the **15 August 2025** deadline to prevent their accounts from being **deactivated** or **blacklisted**.
 
• The initiative is a significant part of the **"One Vehicle, One FASTag"** policy, which aims to streamline the **Electronic Toll Collection (ETC)** process and eliminate the use of multiple tags for a single vehicle.
 
• From the effective date, **telecom and payment aggregators** linked with the **National Electronic Toll Collection (NETC)** will implement stricter verification protocols to enhance the **security** and **transparency** of toll transactions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **FASTag Technology:** 
 
 
• It utilizes **Radio Frequency Identification (RFID)** technology to enable **cashless** and **contactless** payments at toll plazas.
 
• The tag is typically affixed to the **windscreen** of the vehicle and is linked to a **prepaid account** or a **bank account**.
 
 
 
• **Regulatory Authorities:**
 
 
• The **Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH)** oversees the broader policy framework, while **NHAI** manages the physical infrastructure and **IHMCL** handles the digital management of the **FASTag** system.
 
 
 
• **Operational Benefits:**
 
 
• The system significantly reduces **congestion** at **National Highway** toll plazas, thereby saving **fuel** and reducing **CO2 emissions** by minimizing idle time.
 
• It promotes the **Digital India** vision by moving away from manual cash handling and ensuring every rupee collected is **electronically recorded**.
 
 
 
• **Penalty Clauses:**
 
 
• Vehicles entering a **FASTag lane** without a functional tag or with an **invalid/unverified** tag after **15 August 2025** will be liable to pay **double the toll amount** as a penalty.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **KYC Verification:** Users can update their **KYC** through the respective **issuer bank's portal** or the **IHMCL** website. The **RBI** (Reserve Bank of India) guidelines require valid **Identity Proof** and **Address Proof** for this process.
 
• **Global Context:** India's **NETC** program is one of the **world's largest** electronic tolling systems, processing millions of transactions **daily** across over **1,000+** toll plazas nationwide.
 
• **Timeline:** While the **KYC** update requests began earlier in **2024**, the final enforcement of the **annual plan** rules and the **5-year expiry** clause is firmly set for **15 August 2025**.
 
• **Replacement Process:** For tags issued before **2020**, users should proactively contact their **service providers** to receive a new **FASTag** to ensure seamless travel after the implementation date.
</ul

questions.question: At the Bharat Climate Forum 2026, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan stated that effective climate action can help India in which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Strengthening energy security**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• At the **Bharat Climate Forum 2026**, **Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan** emphasized that **effective climate action** is a multi-dimensional strategy that serves as a catalyst for **Strengthening energy security**.
 
• By transitioning from a **fossil-fuel-dependent** economy to one powered by **renewable energy**, India can mitigate the risks associated with volatile global fuel prices and supply chain disruptions. ***Hence, the correct option is Strengthening energy security.***
 
• The focus on **energy security** involves diversifying the **national energy mix** to include **Solar**, **Wind**, and **Green Hydrogen**, which reduces the **import bill** and ensures a steady power supply for industrial and domestic growth.
 
• Climate action in India is intrinsically linked to **self-reliance (Atmanirbhar Bharat)**, where generating clean energy locally protects the nation from geopolitical fluctuations related to **crude oil** and **natural gas** imports.
 
• The speaker highlighted that while **limiting population growth** or **reducing agricultural exports** are different policy domains, **Strengthening energy security** is a direct and logical outcome of proactive environmental stewardship.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Energy Security in India**:
 
 
• India is currently one of the largest consumers of energy globally. Strengthening **Energy Security** is vital for maintaining a high **GDP growth rate**.
 
• The **International Energy Agency (IEA)** has often noted that India’s shift toward **clean energy** is essential for its long-term stability and **economic resilience**.
 
 
 
• **Panchamrit Targets**:
 
 
• India committed to five nectar elements (**Panchamrit**) at **COP26** in **Glasgow**, including achieving **Net Zero** emissions by the year **2070**.
 
• A significant part of this commitment is reaching **500 GW** of non-fossil energy capacity by **2030**, which directly bolsters **energy independence**.
 
 
 
• **National Green Hydrogen Mission**:
 
 
• Launched by the **Government of India** with an initial outlay of **Rs. 19,744 crore**, this mission aims to make India a global hub for **Green Hydrogen** production.
 
• This mission is a cornerstone of **climate action** that replaces **grey hydrogen** and fossil fuels in heavy industries, further **Strengthening energy security**.
 
 
 
• **Role of Renewable Energy**:
 
 
• As of **2024-2025**, India has seen a massive surge in **Installed Capacity** of **Solar Power**. Decentralized solar energy, such as the **PM-KUSUM** scheme, helps farmers gain **energy sovereignty**.
 
• The integration of **Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS)** is another step toward ensuring that **renewable energy** can provide **round-the-clock (RTC)** power, eliminating the need for **coal-based** backup.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Climate Adaptation and Mitigation**: While **mitigation** focuses on reducing **Carbon Footprints**, **adaptation** ensures that infrastructure (including energy grids) is resilient to **climate-induced disasters** like cyclones or floods.
 
• **Economic Impact**: Effective climate action attracts **Green Finance** and **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)** into the **sustainable technology** sector, creating millions of **Green Jobs** by **2030**.
 
• **Global Leadership**: Through initiatives like the **International Solar Alliance (ISA)** and the **Global Biofuels Alliance (GBA)**, India is leading the global south in prioritizing **energy security** through **climate-conscious** collaborations.

questions.question: In 2025, India raised concerns with China regarding the construction of a major upstream hydropower project, urging protection of downstream rights. This project is being developed on which river?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Brahmaputra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Brahmaputra** river, known as the **Yarlung Tsangpo** in the **Tibet Autonomous Region** of **China**, is at the center of a major geopolitical and environmental concern between **India** and **China** in **2025**.
 
• China has moved forward with plans to build a "super dam" in **Medog County**, located near the **Great Bend** where the river turns sharply toward **India**. This project was first formalized under **China's 14th Five-Year Plan (2021-2025)**.
 
• The proposed hydropower station is expected to have a capacity of up to **60 gigawatts (GW)**, which is nearly triple the capacity of the **Three Gorges Dam**, currently the world's largest power station.
 
• In **2025**, **India** raised diplomatic concerns regarding the potential impact on **downstream rights**, specifically fearing that the project could lead to **water diversion**, reduced flow during dry seasons, or **flash floods** during sudden releases.
 
• **India** has consistently urged **China** to ensure that any activity in the **upper reaches** of the river does not harm the interests of downstream states like **India** and **Bangladesh**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Brahmaputra River System:**
 
 
• The river originates from the **Chemayungdung Glacier** of the **Kailash Range** near **Mansarovar Lake** at an elevation of about **5,150 meters**.
 
• It flows for approximately **2,900 km** through three countries: **China (Tibet)**, **India**, and **Bangladesh**. In **India**, it enters through **Arunachal Pradesh**, where it is known as the **Siang** or **Dihang**, before flowing through the **Assam Valley**.
 
 
 
• **Downstream Impact and Counter-Measures:**
 
 
• To mitigate the risks posed by upstream Chinese dams, the **Government of India** has planned a massive **11,000 MW** hydropower project on the **Siang River** in **Arunachal Pradesh** to create a water storage buffer.
 
• The **Brahmaputra** carries a significant amount of **silt** and is vital for the **biodiversity** of the **northeast region** of **India**, including the **Kaziranga National Park**.
 
 
 
• **Transboundary River Agreements:**
 
 
• Unlike the **Indus Waters Treaty (1960)** between **India** and **Pakistan**, there is no formal water-sharing treaty between **India** and **China**.
 
• Currently, cooperation is limited to a **Memorandum of Understanding (MoU)** where **China** provides hydrological data (water level and discharge) during the monsoon season from **May 15th** to **October 15th**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Transboundary Rivers:**
 
 
• **Sutlej:** Also originates in **Tibet** (as the **Langqen Zangbo**) and enters **India** through the **Shipki La** pass. While **China** builds dams here too, it is part of the **Indus system**.
 
• **Indus:** Originates near **Lake Mansarovar** and flows through **Ladakh** before entering **Pakistan**. It is governed by a strict bilateral treaty.
 
• **Kosi:** Known as the "Sorrow of Bihar," it is a transboundary river flowing through **China (Tibet)**, **Nepal**, and **India**, primarily known for its high **sediment load** and course changes.
 
 
 
• **Geopolitical Context:** The construction of dams on the **Brahmaputra** is often viewed through the lens of "water wars" or strategic leverage, as **India** occupies the **middle reach** and **Bangladesh** the **lower reach**, making them vulnerable to upstream interventions in the **Tibet** region.
</ul

questions.question: On which date is Birsa Munda Martyr’s Day observed, as commemorated every year?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**9th June**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Birsa Munda Martyr’s Day** is observed every year on **9th June** to pay tribute to the iconic tribal leader and freedom fighter who died on this day in **1900**.
 
• He passed away while in British custody at the **Ranchi Jail** at the young age of **25**. While the official records cited **cholera** as the cause of death, many believe he was poisoned by the colonial authorities.
 
• Birsa Munda spearheaded the **Munda Rebellion**, which is famously known as the **Ulgulan** or the **Great Tumult**, in the **Chhota Nagpur** plateau region (modern-day **Jharkhand**) during the late **1890s**.
 
• The rebellion was directed against the **British Raj** and the **Dikus** (outsiders like landlords and moneylenders) who were exploiting the tribal communities and seizing their ancestral lands.
 
• His powerful resistance eventually forced the colonial government to enact the **Chhota Nagpur Tenancy Act, 1908**, which prohibited the transfer of tribal land to non-tribal people, ensuring a degree of land security for the **Adivasis**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Early Life and Birth**: Birsa Munda was born on **November 15, 1875**, in the village of **Ulihatu** in the **Khunti** district of present-day **Jharkhand**.
 
• **Janjatiya Gaurav Divas**: In **2021**, the **Government of India** declared **November 15** (his birth anniversary) as **Janjatiya Gaurav Divas** (Tribal Pride Day) to recognize the historical contributions of tribal heroes.
 
• **Religious Leadership**: He founded a new faith called **Birsait**, which promoted monotheism and urged the Munda people to return to their original religious roots, shunning animal sacrifice, alcohol, and witchcraft.
 
• **Revered Titles**: Due to his charismatic leadership and spiritual influence, he is affectionately called **Dharti Aba** (Father of Earth) and is worshipped as **Bhagwan Birsa Munda** by tribal communities across **India**.
 
• **Legacy**: Birsa Munda is the only tribal leader whose portrait hangs in the **Central Hall of the Indian Parliament**, symbolizing his immense importance in the **Indian Independence Movement**.
 
• **Museum**: The **Bhagwan Birsa Munda Memorial Park cum Freedom Fighter Museum** was inaugurated in **Ranchi** in **November 2021** to preserve the history of tribal struggles.
